craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of identity stated; vyabhicāri exultation (utsāha) at aloneness doubled. Sanskrit-first: sa eva (HE ALONE — eva insisted); aiśvarya-rūpa (LORDSHIP-MADE — sovereignty as the world's form). Rows: 9 (He-alone/His-alone echo), 1 (‘Lordship-made’ closes — formed-ness last), 3 (aloneness interlock: He-alone…His-alone). Close: ‘His power, Lordship-made’. Rupture: semicolon (who turns to what-all). Rejected: ‘His very own power’ — killed: doubles ‘alone’ weakly; ‘the universe’ — killed: ‘whole host of things’ kept inventoried; ‘is the self of all’ — killed: svabhāva kept own-nature (technical). Read aloud: HE a-LONE is EV-ery BE-ing's OWN-na-ture … WHOLE-host OF-things — HIS-pow-er, LORD-ship-MADE.

lines: He alone is every being's own-nature, the supreme Lord;
and the whole host of things — His power, Lordship-made.
l4.sanskrit_cite: sa eva sarvabhūtānāṃ svabhāvaḥ parameśvaraḥ | bhāvajātaṃ hi tasyaiva śaktir īśvaratāmayī

reads_against.argmap: Who is own-nature of all beings? → Identity, not process: He alone beings' nature; all things His Lordship-shaped power.
c1_essence: He alone beings' own-nature; the world's abundance power cast as sovereignty.
